pathway.title: Dream Finders Homes, Inc. — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: Leverage is high and rose fast, and the issuer's own EBITDA flatters it. Net debt of USD 1,750.37 million was 4.69x last-twelve-months EBITDA at 30 September 2026, against 1.61x at the end of 2024, and EBITDA covered cash interest paid only 1.23x; pro forma net debt for the Beazer acquisition of 20 October 2026 is not established. The issuer's EBITDA adds back interest charged to cost of sales, which is 56.15% of the last-twelve-months figure, and without that add-back net debt would be 10.69x EBITDA, so a lender using a stricter definition sees a much weaker position. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 70; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 51; calculation C3; calculation C6

The business does not yet turn earnings into free cash flow, so growth is funded with debt. Operating cash flow was negative in every period reported, and after capital expenditure free cash flow was negative by USD 281,993 thousand in 2024, USD 126,366 thousand in 2025 and USD 320,552 thousand in the first nine months of 2026. Inventory purchases in nine months were 52.51% larger than a year earlier, and negative free cash flow explains 84.59% of the rise in net debt, rising to 97.47% with buybacks and preferred dividends. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 89; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 6; calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C3; calculation C4

Earnings are falling faster than revenue because margin is compressing. Revenue fell 5.24% in nine months but EBITDA fell 33.68% and pre-tax income fell 66.59%, homebuilding gross margin was 14.5% against 17.7%, the average selling price fell 7.71% and backlog value fell 8.72%. Management has cut compensation costs and can drop land options, but the cuts have not offset higher land and financing costs, and each percentage point of homebuilding gross margin is worth 10.57% of last-twelve-months EBITDA. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 39; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 42; calculation C5; calculation C13; calculation C15

Liquidity was thin before the acquisition closed, and its level after closing is not established. Total liquidity, cash plus revolver availability, fell 42.03% from the end of 2025 to 30 September 2026 and covered 15.42 months at the nine-month rate of operating cash outflow before the acquisition closed. Availability under the Credit Agreement is set by a borrowing base rather than by its commitments, and the amount drawn at closing is not stated. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 73; EX99.1_2026-09-30_dfh_dfh-q32026xer-htm.htm.jsonl, page 1; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 12; calculation C7

Refinancing risk is concentrated in August 2028 and starts earlier. USD 300.0 million of Credit Agreement commitments mature on 4 June 2027, and the commitments of USD 1,200.0 million and the senior notes of USD 300.0 million fall due within a week of each other in August 2028, about 21 months after the as-of date. From the stated commitments, USD 1,199.0 million to USD 1,499.0 million of debt, 60.07% to 75.10% of total debt before the acquisition, matures in that week; this is an analyst bound because the split of drawings between tranches is not stated. Market access is shown but costly: the company raised USD 652.4 million of net Series B proceeds and USD 572.1 million of land bank proceeds in September and October 2026, at a 12.0% preferred dividend and by trading land for option rights. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 30; 10-K_2025-12-31_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 74; calculation C8

The Beazer acquisition raises fixed charges before it adds earnings, and its net effect on leverage is not established. The assumed Beazer notes carry USD 50.75 million of annual coupon and the Series B stock a 12.0% dividend of USD 81.0 million a year, together USD 131.75 million, equal to 35.29% of last-twelve-months EBITDA and 43.30% of last-twelve-months cash interest, before any change in earnings. The enterprise value is 52.38% of pre-closing total assets. Management targets over USD 100 million of annual cost synergies, equal to 26.79% of the same EBITDA, and a return to current leverage metrics within 18 to 24 months, but gives no figure. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); EX99.1_2026-06-30_dfh_ex-991pressreleasexmergera-htm.htm.jsonl, page 3; EX99.1_2026-06-30_dfh_ex-991pressreleasexmergera-htm.htm.jsonl, page 4; EX99.1_2026-09-30_dfh_ex991closingpr-htm.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation C10; calculation C11; calculation C14

Financial policy is a mixed signal, with no common dividend but concentrated control and pledged shares that add event risk. The founder holds about 84% of the votes, 61.50% of his Class B stock was pledged at the end of 2025 against 30.32% a year earlier, and Series B holders can demand cash if his holding falls below 50% of votes or economic interest. Business & governance rates governance risk medium, and this module agrees because the pledge is an event risk rather than a cash drain on the company today. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 48; 10-K_2025-12-31_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 49; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 26; calculation C15

The nearest test is the fourth quarter, and the guidance looks demanding. The full-year closings guidance needs a fourth quarter 23.15% above the fourth quarter of 2025 and 1.59x the third quarter of 2026, against 1.32x a year earlier, and backlog homes due in 2026 cover only 48.96% of the closings required. A miss would lower earnings into a larger debt base while the acquisition adds fixed charges. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 62; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 39; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 48; EX99.1_2026-09-30_dfh_dfh-q32026xer-htm.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation C9

cells.text: Designs, builds and sells single-family homes in high-growth markets, from entry level to active adult, and sells homes to investors under built-for-rent contracts; mortgage, title and insurance services support the homebuyer
Earnings follow housing demand and mortgage rates, so cash generation is cyclical

Asset-light: finished lot options and land bank options with lot deposits that average about 10% of the land price; lot deposits USD 490 million and 52,574 controlled lots at 2026-09-30; risk of loss USD 808 million against USD 773 million at 2025-12-31
Keeps owned land low and limits losses to deposits and fees, but fees rise when lot takedowns are delayed and the pipeline is under review after Beazer
Southeast, Mid-Atlantic and Midwest homebuilding plus Financial Services; share of 2026 nine-month revenue 34.10%, 24.83%, 35.60% and 5.47%
No homebuilding segment above 36% of revenue; the Midwest is largest and had the largest revenue fall
Home closings 6,127 against 6,072; average sales price USD 447,830 against USD 485,216, down 7.71%; net sales 6,352 against 5,991, up 6%
Volume holds while price falls, which compresses margin per home
Homebuilding gross margin 14.5% against 17.7%; adjusted homebuilding gross margin 24.2% against 26.8% (issuer non-GAAP measure)
The margin cushion that supports interest cover is thinner before the acquisition adds interest
Backlog 2,064 homes worth USD 1,068,946 thousand at 2026-09-30 against 2,619 homes worth USD 1,171,041 thousand a year earlier; active communities 365 against 283
Backlog value down 8.72% gives less forward revenue visibility despite more communities

Mortgage banking through Jet HomeLoans, title agency through DF Title, title underwriting through Alliant Title and homeowners insurance; segment revenue USD 161,169 thousand and income before taxes USD 28,958 thousand
5.47% of revenue; mortgage loans are financed by warehouse lines that sit inside total debt but are matched to loans held for sale
1,911 full-time employees at 2025-12-31, 395 in financial services; homebuilding SG&A fell mainly on lower compensation cost of USD 21 million, mostly from headcount and other reductions
Overhead cuts support margin but follow weaker results
Announced footprint of 26 markets and about 520 active communities after closing; Beazer adds California, Nevada, Indiana and Delaware
Management expectation, not yet in reported figures; adds geographic diversification and integration load

runs.text: - Strength: Asset-light land supply limits capital tied up in land. Option contracts cap the loss on land at deposits and fees, with USD 808 million at risk at 30 September 2026, and let the company terminate options that miss its return thresholds, which gives it a lever to cut spending if demand weakens. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 43; EX99.1_2026-09-30_dfh_dfh-q32026xer-htm.htm.jsonl, page 2; Business & governance (CP-1A)

- Strength: Scale and regional breadth spread the demand risk. No homebuilding segment is more than 35.60% of nine-month revenue, closings were a record for the period, and the acquisition adds new states, which softens a local downturn. Basis: EX99.1_2026-09-30_dfh_dfh-q32026xer-htm.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX99.1_2026-09-30_dfh_ex991closingpr-htm.htm.jsonl, page 2; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C15

- Strength: Integrated financial services add a second earnings stream. Mortgage capture was 81.1% in nine months and financial services were 5.47% of revenue, which supports closings and diversifies income, though it is small against the debt. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 49; Business & governance (CP-1A)

- Strength: Access to capital has held in a weak market. The company raised USD 652.4 million of net Series B proceeds and USD 572.1 million of land bank proceeds, which funded part of the acquisition, and it has paid no common dividend. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 25; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 30; 10-K_2025-12-31_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 53; calculation C15

- Weakness: Leverage and cover are weak and weakening. Net debt was 4.69x last-twelve-months EBITDA and EBITDA covered cash interest 1.23x before the acquisition, which leaves little room for an earnings fall, and pro forma figures are not established. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C6

- Weakness: Free cash flow is negative and debt funds the gap. Free cash flow was negative by USD 320,552 thousand in nine months, with inventory purchases 52.51% larger, so growth adds debt instead of cash. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C3

- Weakness: Margin and order book are shrinking. Gross margin fell to 14.5% from 17.7% and backlog value fell 8.72%, so earnings per home and forward revenue are both lower. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 39; calculation C5; calculation C15

- Weakness: Refinancing is concentrated in August 2028. Between 60.07% and 75.10% of pre-closing debt falls due in one week, after USD 300.0 million of commitments mature in June 2027, so the company depends on market access in 2027 and 2028. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 11; calculation C8

- Weakness: Founder control, pledged shares and a senior preferred claim add event risk. 61.50% of the founder's Class B stock was pledged at the end of 2025, and a fall in his holding below 50% of votes or economic interest lets Series B holders demand cash. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C15

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: Dream Finders acquired Beazer Homes USA, Inc. in an all-cash merger signed on 6 August 2026 and completed on 20 October 2026, 75 days later, at USD 33.50 per Beazer share and an enterprise value of about USD 2.2 billion. The offer history published on 11 May 2026 ran from USD 28.50 per share on 5 February to USD 29.00 on 17 March and USD 25.75 on 5 May, so the agreed price is 30.10% above the last of these; management puts the price at an implied 0.8x of Beazer's book value. Management calls it the ninth acquisition since the 2021 listing and by far the largest, and it adds California, Nevada, Indiana and Delaware to the footprint. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 7; EX99.1_2026-03-31_dfh_ex-991pressrelease-htm.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX99.1_2026-03-31_dfh_ex-991pressrelease-htm.htm.jsonl, page 5; EX99.1_2026-03-31_dfh_ex-991pressrelease-htm.htm.jsonl, page 6; EX99.1_2026-03-31_dfh_ex-991pressrelease-htm.htm.jsonl, page 8; EX99.1_2026-06-30_dfh_ex-991pressreleasexmergera-htm.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX99.1_2026-09-30_dfh_ex991closingpr-htm.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation C16; calculation C28

Funding came from cash on hand, borrowings under the Credit Agreement and Series B preferred stock proceeds. The second closing of Series B on 20 October 2026 raised USD 435.3 million net of USD 450.0 million, after a first closing on 14 September 2026 of USD 217.1 million net that mainly redeemed the Series A stock. On 20 October 2026 a land bank facility paid USD 572.1 million for pre-acquisition Beazer land sold to Millrose, with an option for Dream Finders to buy the homesites later; the proceeds redeemed Beazer's USD 350.0 million 7.25% notes due 2029, repaid its unsecured credit facility and paid transaction costs. On 9 October 2026 the company asked to raise Credit Agreement commitments by USD 220.0 million to about USD 1.7 billion. The amount drawn under the Credit Agreement at closing is not stated. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 25; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 29; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 30; calculation C10; calculation C17; calculation C18; calculation C20

Beazer's USD 250.0 million 7.5% notes due 2031 and USD 400.0 million 8.0% notes due 2032 were assumed at closing. On 22 October 2026 Dream Finders offered new notes of its own with the same interest, maturity and redemption terms in exchange, with a consent solicitation to remove substantially all restrictive covenants and events of default from the Beazer indentures. Holders of 98.64% of the principal had tendered by 4 November 2026; for each USD 1,000 tendered by that date they receive USD 1,000 of new notes and USD 1.00 in cash, and later tenders receive USD 950 of new notes. The offers expire on 20 November 2026 unless extended, and settlement is expected on 23 November 2026, after the as-of date. The guarantors, ranking and covenants of the new notes are not stated in the documents supplied. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 30; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 31; EX99.1_2026-09-30_dfh_pr-exchangeofferxlaunch-htm.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX99.1_2026-09-30_dfh_pr-exchangeofferxlaunch-htm.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX99.1_2026-09-30_dfh_pr-exchangeofferxearlypart-htm.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX99.1_2026-09-30_dfh_pr-exchangeofferxearlypart-htm.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation C17; calculation C19

Management's stated aims are over USD 100 million of annual run-rate cost synergies, double-digit percentage earnings per share accretion in the first year and a return to or improvement on current leverage metrics within 18 to 24 months; these are management language and no pro forma debt figure is given. The Credit Agreement amendment of 22 September 2026 raised the letter of credit sublimit from USD 25.0 million to USD 100.0 million and modified covenants on land bank transactions, asset dispositions and obligations assumed in permitted acquisitions. The agreement also lets the maximum debt to capitalization ratio rise temporarily from 60.0% to 65.0% for the quarter in which a material acquisition completes and the next three quarters. Basis: EX99.1_2026-06-30_dfh_ex-991pressreleasexmergera-htm.htm.jsonl, page 3; EX99.1_2026-06-30_dfh_ex-991pressreleasexmergera-htm.htm.jsonl, page 4; EX99.1_2026-09-30_dfh_ex991closingpr-htm.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 12

fields.value: Net debt reached 4.69x last-twelve-months EBITDA at 30 September 2026, up from 1.61x at the end of 2024, and EBITDA covered cash interest paid only 1.23x, which leaves creditors little cushion before the Beazer acquisition adds further debt.

fields.value: The issuer's EBITDA adds back interest charged to homebuilding cost of sales, which makes up 56.15% of last-twelve-months EBITDA against 29.75% for 2024, so these ratios depend on that definition and a lender who excludes the add-back sees much weaker coverage.

fields.value: Pro forma net debt for the Beazer acquisition that closed on 20 October 2026 is not established: the sources give USD 435.3 million of Series B preferred proceeds and USD 572.1 million of land bank proceeds, but not the Credit Agreement drawing at closing, Beazer's cash or how the land bank funding is recorded.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The maturity ladder is also not established, because the sources give no maturity dates for the warehouse lines or other borrowings and do not split the revolver drawings between its two tranches.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The Beazer acquisition closed on 2026-10-20, after the 2026-09-30 balance sheet, and no period figure includes it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The second closing of the Series B preferred stock and the land bank facility funding both occurred on 2026-10-20, the request to raise Credit Agreement commitments by USD 220.0 million was made on 2026-10-09, and the exchange offers for Beazer's notes began on 2026-10-22 with settlement expected on 2026-11-23; all of these are after the balance sheet and are kept out of the period figures.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The ratios use the issuer's own EBITDA, which adds back interest charged to cost of sales, and total debt that includes mortgage warehouse borrowings, so they are not comparable with ratios built on EBITDA after that interest or on homebuilding debt alone.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash paid for interest is a single printed figure that is not split between interest capitalized into inventory and interest expensed, so cover is read against it as printed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Undrawn availability is set by the borrowing base after the senior notes, not by the commitments, and the 2026-09-30 figure is before any Beazer assets entered the base.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The ladder is empty because the sources date only the notes and the two revolver tranches, not the warehouse lines, the other borrowings or the revolver drawings by tranche; the dated maturities are in the debt instruments table and nothing is estimated here.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Every row covers twelve months, and the Adjusted EBITDA column is empty because the issuer states only its own reported EBITDA, which the register and statements carry.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Other borrowings of 38.706 are left out because no source states their security or ranking, so the rows total 1,957.309 of the 1,996.015 of total debt, and preferred stock, leases and off-balance-sheet bonds are outside the stack.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No bridge is drawn because there is no adjusted measure; the reconciliation from net income to the issuer's EBITDA is in the income statement table.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The maturity ladder is not established: the sources give no maturity dates for the mortgage warehouse lines or other borrowings and do not split the revolver drawings between the tranches maturing on 2027-06-04 and 2028-08-21, so every maturity cell and the contractual principal are shown as not supplied. Severity: High. Action: obtain the warehouse terms and the drawn amount by tranche from the executed credit agreement.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Pro forma net debt and net leverage after the Beazer acquisition are not established: the sources do not state the Credit Agreement drawing at closing, Beazer's cash and debt at closing, or whether the USD 572.1 million of land bank proceeds is recorded as debt or a sale, so the post-balance-sheet rows give amounts only where the sources state them. Severity: High. Action: obtain the closing-date balance sheet or pro forma statements.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Covenant levels after the amendments of 2026-07-02 and 2026-09-22 are not established: the executed agreement is not supplied and the 2025 annual report states the five tests only as at 2025-12-31. Severity: Medium. Action: obtain the executed amendments.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No adjusted EBITDA is stated by the issuer, so the adjusted EBITDA row, the adjusted ratios and the EBITDA bridge are shown as not supplied. Severity: Low. Action: none needed unless the issuer begins to state one.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Other borrowings of USD 38.706 million at 2026-09-30 are not itemised: their security, ranking, rate and maturity are not stated and only USD 23.394 million is identified as secured, so this row is left out of the debt stack and its principal is not supplied. Severity: Medium. Action: obtain the composition from the issuer.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Cash paid for interest is one printed figure with no split between interest capitalized into inventory and interest expensed, and the filings do not say whether it includes lot option fees; the cover ratios use it as printed. Severity: Medium. Action: ask the issuer for the split.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - EBITDA is the issuer's own non-GAAP measure and includes an add-back of interest charged to homebuilding cost of sales, which is 56.15% of last-twelve-months EBITDA; no independent EBITDA is built and the effect is quantified in the definition register. Severity: High. Action: read every leverage and cover figure beside the EBITDA before the add-back.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The 2025-09-30 balance sheet is only partly printed, with total debt, cash, mezzanine equity and equity but not total assets or total liabilities, so there is no 9M 2025 balance sheet column and no 2025-09-30 leverage ratio. Severity: Low. Action: obtain the third-quarter 2025 quarterly report if that date is needed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Lines printed as dashes are shown as not supplied and never as zero: contingent consideration in 9M 2026, the 2024 interest expense in the EBITDA reconciliation, payments for acquisitions in 9M 2026, deposits on pending acquisitions after 2024, investment securities in 2024, senior note proceeds in 2024 and 9M 2026, and the other nil financing lines; the totals add without them. Severity: Low. Action: none.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Lines printed only in the interim statements (gains on equity securities, preferred stock issuance and redemption, and borrowings related to consolidated inventory not owned) are not supplied for the annual columns, and the contingent consideration line is not printed on the 2026-09-30 balance sheet. Severity: Low. Action: none.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Capital expenditure is printed only as one line, so no split between maintenance and growth is supplied. Severity: Low. Action: none.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The fourth quarter of 2025 is not printed and is derived as the fiscal year less nine months; it is labelled calculated and replaces no reported period. Severity: Low. Action: none.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Claims outside total debt are stated but not in the ratios: redeemable preferred stock of USD 218.875 million, lease liabilities of USD 27.503 million at 2025-12-31 with no later figure stated, surety bonds of USD 347.6 million and letters of credit of USD 25.1 million at 2026-09-30. fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Business and governance for Dream Finders Homes, Inc., issuer dfh-1825088, as of 2026-11-18 on the credit snapshot pathway: the business, ownership and control, the Beazer transaction and its funding, and governance and capital allocation behavior, on the supplied documents to 2026-11-05.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Dream Finders is a founder-controlled, asset-light homebuilder whose USD 2.2 billion Beazer acquisition adds debt, 12.0% preferred stock and land bank funding while margins fall, and governance gives creditors little independent restraint. The founder holds about 84% of the votes and had pledged 61.50% of his Class B stock for margin loans at the end of 2025, against 30.32% a year earlier, and a fall below 50% of votes or economic interest would let Series B holders demand cash.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Offsetting this, the land model limits owned land, no common dividend has ever been paid and the board added homebuilding leadership in 2026, so governance risk is medium rather than high; pro forma debt and liquidity are not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Control is concentrated in one person and part of it is financed by pledged shares, so a market-driven forced sale is the main route by which control could change. The founder holds all Class B stock and about 84% of the votes. The share of his Class B stock pledged for margin loans rose from 30.32% at the end of 2024 to 61.50% at the end of 2025, and a further 5.20% was under prepaid forward sale contracts. The lender, loan size and trigger prices are not disclosed. On a simple count of common shares he could part with about 21.58% of his Class B stock before his holding fell to 50% of common shares outstanding, which is well below the share pledged.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The Series B preferred stock ties the founder's holding to a cash claim on the company. Holders can require redemption in cash at the greater of the as-converted value and the liquidation preference, plus accrued dividends, if the founder ceases to own at least 50% of both the voting power and the economic interest, or on a change of control. The face value is USD 675.0 million and the 12.0% cumulative dividend is USD 81.0 million a year, against USD 13.5 million a year on the redeemed 9% Series A stock. The company may defer dividends, which protects cash but compounds the claim at 12.0%. The stock is classified as mezzanine equity and ranks ahead of common stock.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Board independence is not established, and the exemptions open to a controlled company remain available. The company is a controlled company under exchange rules and may opt out of independent-majority and committee requirements; it says it has not used the exemptions at this time. A Co-Chairman with long homebuilding experience and an independent director joined the board in July 2026 and a chief operating officer started in June 2026, which strengthens operating oversight, but the founder remains chief executive and the other Co-Chairman. Which directors are independent is not stated in the documents supplied. The company also reincorporated in Texas on 9 June 2026, and the effect on stockholder and creditor protections is not stated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Related-party dealings look modest, but the supply of lots leans on related funds. The company leased an aircraft from a company the founder owns at a cost of USD 4.6 million in 2025. It owns 49.0% of the manager of the land bank funds that supply lots, and officers invest in those funds. Lot deposits with the two related funds were USD 61.6 million at 30 September 2026, 12.57% of all lot deposits, and the company and key executives have committed USD 57.6 million to the newest fund, of which 55.9% has been funded. How the funds' lot terms compare with third-party terms is not disclosed, so pricing leakage cannot be tested.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The operating model limits capital tied up in land but leaves the company exposed to weak demand, and the numbers worsened through 2026. Option deposits, fees and pre-acquisition costs put USD 808 million at risk at 30 September 2026, up 4.53% from year end, while the controlled lot pipeline fell 16.71%. Homebuilding gross margin was 14.5% in the first nine months of 2026 against 17.7% a year earlier, the average selling price fell 7.71% and backlog value fell 8.72%. Closings and net sales were records for the period, with net sales up 6%, so volume is holding at lower prices and margins. Total liquidity, cash plus revolver availability, fell 42.07% from year end to USD 521 million before the acquisition closed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The Beazer acquisition is the largest single event for creditors, and its effect on debt is not established. The enterprise value of about USD 2.2 billion equals 52.38% of the company's total assets and 1.10x its total debt before closing, and the agreed price was 30.10% above the last public proposal and 15.52% above the highest earlier one. Funding came from cash on hand, Credit Agreement borrowings, USD 435.3 million of second-closing preferred stock and USD 572.1 million of land bank proceeds, and USD 650.0 million of Beazer notes were assumed; the amount drawn under the Credit Agreement and Beazer's cash at closing are not stated. Management says leverage will return to or improve on current metrics within 18 to 24 months but gives no figure, and an earlier statement said the effect on leverage would be minimal.

Holders of 98.64% of the Beazer notes had tendered by the early date and delivered consents that remove substantially all restrictive covenants from those notes, and settlement is expected on 23 November 2026, after the as-of date. fields.value: Payouts to shareholders have been modest, but repurchases continued while debt rose. No common dividend has ever been paid. The company repurchased USD 39.3 million of Class A stock in the first nine months of 2026, up 20.18% on the year before, leaving USD 11.1 million of the USD 100.0 million authorization, and made no purchases in September. It redeemed the 9% Series A at 101.0% of face for USD 154.3 million using Series B proceeds, replacing a 9% claim with a 12.0% one.

fields.value: Disclosure supports monitoring, but the executed financing and preferred stock documents are not supplied. The auditor's opinions on the 2025 statements and on internal control were clean, and its critical audit matter was the indicators of inventory impairment. Management expects deal abandonment charges in the fourth quarter as it reviews the combined land pipeline, and the quarterly report says the review may produce material charges.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a cautious view is structural. The company has never paid a common dividend and the option model keeps owned land low. The insider trading policy was tightened between 2024 and 2025 so that pledges now need board approval without the requesting person's vote. The Series B stock lets the company defer dividends to protect cash. Management states the purchase price was an implied 0.8x of Beazer's book value and expects over USD 100 million of annual run-rate cost synergies, and net sales were a record for the first nine months of 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The view would move toward lower risk if the company disclosed pro forma debt and liquidity that match the 18 to 24 month deleveraging commitment, margin loan terms with ample headroom, a board majority confirmed as independent, or a lower pledge. It would move toward higher risk if pledged shares were sold or called, if the Credit Agreement were drawn heavily at closing, if the land pipeline review produced large abandonment charges, or if gross margin fell further below the 14.5% reported for the first nine months of 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Dream Finders acquired Beazer Homes USA, Inc. in an all-cash merger signed on 6 August 2026 and completed on 20 October 2026, 75 days later, at USD 33.50 per Beazer share and an enterprise value of about USD 2.2 billion. The offer history published on 11 May 2026 ran from USD 28.50 per share on 5 February to USD 29.00 on 17 March and USD 25.75 on 5 May, so the agreed price is 30.10% above the last of these; management puts the price at an implied 0.8x of Beazer's book value. Management calls it the ninth acquisition since the 2021 listing and by far the largest, and it adds California, Nevada, Indiana and Delaware to the footprint.

fields.value: Funding came from cash on hand, borrowings under the Credit Agreement and Series B preferred stock proceeds. The second closing of Series B on 20 October 2026 raised USD 435.3 million net of USD 450.0 million, after a first closing on 14 September 2026 of USD 217.1 million net that mainly redeemed the Series A stock. On 20 October 2026 a land bank facility paid USD 572.1 million for pre-acquisition Beazer land sold to Millrose, with an option for Dream Finders to buy the homesites later; the proceeds redeemed Beazer's USD 350.0 million 7.25% notes due 2029, repaid its unsecured credit facility and paid transaction costs. On 9 October 2026 the company asked to raise Credit Agreement commitments by USD 220.0 million to about USD 1.7 billion. The amount drawn under the Credit Agreement at closing is not stated.

The Credit Agreement amendment of 22 September 2026 raised the letter of credit sublimit from USD 25.0 million to USD 100.0 million and modified covenants on land bank transactions, asset dispositions and obligations assumed in permitted acquisitions. fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Sponsor / Governance Risk Level: Medium. The level is driven by founder control with pledged shares and by a large debt-funded acquisition, because both raise event and leverage risk for creditors, which implies close monitoring rather than a restrictive view. Countervailing evidence is the absence of common dividends, of fees to the controlling holder beyond the aircraft lease and of any action against existing noteholders. Further analysis requires the proxy statement, the margin loan terms and pro forma debt.

fields.value: Fundamental credit for Dream Finders Homes, Inc., issuer dfh-1825088, as of 2026-11-18 on the credit snapshot pathway: the overall credit profile, its strongest support, its weakest dimension and its primary downside path, using the supplied documents to 2026-11-05 and the financial foundation and business and governance work on them.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Dream Finders has a weak and weakening credit profile: net leverage reached 4.69x and interest cover 1.23x before the Beazer acquisition, cash is consumed in every period, and creditors depend on a housing recovery and on refinancing in August 2028. Pro forma net leverage after the closing on 20 October 2026 is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The business is adequate rather than weak: the asset-light land model, three regional segments and record closings give volume, but homebuilding gross margin fell from 17.7% to 14.5% and total liquidity fell 42.03% in nine months, so a deal funded with debt, 12.0% preferred stock and land bank proceeds raises the stakes.

fields.name: Quote

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage is high and rose fast, and the issuer's own EBITDA flatters it. Net debt of USD 1,750.37 million was 4.69x last-twelve-months EBITDA at 30 September 2026, against 1.61x at the end of 2024, and EBITDA covered cash interest paid only 1.23x; pro forma net debt for the Beazer acquisition of 20 October 2026 is not established. The issuer's EBITDA adds back interest charged to cost of sales, which is 56.15% of the last-twelve-months figure, and without that add-back net debt would be 10.69x EBITDA, so a lender using a stricter definition sees a much weaker position.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 70; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 51; calculation C3; calculation C6

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The business does not yet turn earnings into free cash flow, so growth is funded with debt. Operating cash flow was negative in every period reported, and after capital expenditure free cash flow was negative by USD 281,993 thousand in 2024, USD 126,366 thousand in 2025 and USD 320,552 thousand in the first nine months of 2026. Inventory purchases in nine months were 52.51% larger than a year earlier, and negative free cash flow explains 84.59% of the rise in net debt, rising to 97.47% with buybacks and preferred dividends.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 89; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 6; calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C3; calculation C4

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Earnings are falling faster than revenue because margin is compressing. Revenue fell 5.24% in nine months but EBITDA fell 33.68% and pre-tax income fell 66.59%, homebuilding gross margin was 14.5% against 17.7%, the average selling price fell 7.71% and backlog value fell 8.72%. Management has cut compensation costs and can drop land options, but the cuts have not offset higher land and financing costs, and each percentage point of homebuilding gross margin is worth 10.57% of last-twelve-months EBITDA.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity was thin before the acquisition closed, and its level after closing is not established. Total liquidity, cash plus revolver availability, fell 42.03% from the end of 2025 to 30 September 2026 and covered 15.42 months at the nine-month rate of operating cash outflow before the acquisition closed. Availability under the Credit Agreement is set by a borrowing base rather than by its commitments, and the amount drawn at closing is not stated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Refinancing risk is concentrated in August 2028 and starts earlier. USD 300.0 million of Credit Agreement commitments mature on 4 June 2027, and the commitments of USD 1,200.0 million and the senior notes of USD 300.0 million fall due within a week of each other in August 2028, about 21 months after the as-of date. From the stated commitments, USD 1,199.0 million to USD 1,499.0 million of debt, 60.07% to 75.10% of total debt before the acquisition, matures in that week; this is an analyst bound because the split of drawings between tranches is not stated. Market access is shown but costly: the company raised USD 652.4 million of net Series B proceeds and USD 572.1 million of land bank proceeds in September and October 2026, at a 12.0% preferred dividend and by trading land for option rights.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The Beazer acquisition raises fixed charges before it adds earnings, and its net effect on leverage is not established. The assumed Beazer notes carry USD 50.75 million of annual coupon and the Series B stock a 12.0% dividend of USD 81.0 million a year, together USD 131.75 million, equal to 35.29% of last-twelve-months EBITDA and 43.30% of last-twelve-months cash interest, before any change in earnings. The enterprise value is 52.38% of pre-closing total assets. Management targets over USD 100 million of annual cost synergies, equal to 26.79% of the same EBITDA, and a return to current leverage metrics within 18 to 24 months, but gives no figure.

fields.value: Financial policy is a mixed signal, with no common dividend but concentrated control and pledged shares that add event risk. The founder holds about 84% of the votes, 61.50% of his Class B stock was pledged at the end of 2025 against 30.32% a year earlier, and Series B holders can demand cash if his holding falls below 50% of votes or economic interest. Business & governance rates governance risk medium, and this module agrees because the pledge is an event risk rather than a cash drain on the company today.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The nearest test is the fourth quarter, and the guidance looks demanding. The full-year closings guidance needs a fourth quarter 23.15% above the fourth quarter of 2025 and 1.59x the third quarter of 2026, against 1.32x a year earlier, and backlog homes due in 2026 cover only 48.96% of the closings required. A miss would lower earnings into a larger debt base while the acquisition adds fixed charges.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a weak view is flexibility and access to capital. The asset-light model lets the company drop land options and caps its loss on them at deposits and fees, closings and net sales were records for the period, and the company raised USD 652.4 million of net preferred proceeds and USD 572.1 million of land bank proceeds in a weak market. Management says the purchase price was an implied 0.8x of Beazer's book value and targets over USD 100 million of annual cost synergies, and the Credit Agreement temporarily allows debt to capitalization of 65.0% instead of 60.0% after a material acquisition.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The view would improve if pro forma debt and liquidity showed leverage near the pre-closing level, if operating cash flow turned positive as inventory is sold, if homebuilding gross margin held above 14.5% and if the 2027 commitments were extended. It would worsen if fourth-quarter closings missed the guidance, if gross margin fell again by 3.2 percentage points, which would lift net leverage to 7.08x and cut cover to 0.81x before closing, if liquidity after closing proved thinner than the 15.42 months of pre-closing runway, or if pledged founder shares were sold.

fields.value: - Strength: Scale and regional breadth spread the demand risk. No homebuilding segment is more than 35.60% of nine-month revenue, closings were a record for the period, and the acquisition adds new states, which softens a local downturn.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Strength: Integrated financial services add a second earnings stream. Mortgage capture was 81.1% in nine months and financial services were 5.47% of revenue, which supports closings and diversifies income, though it is small against the debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Strength: Access to capital has held in a weak market. The company raised USD 652.4 million of net Series B proceeds and USD 572.1 million of land bank proceeds, which funded part of the acquisition, and it has paid no common dividend.

fields.value: - Weakness: Leverage and cover are weak and weakening. Net debt was 4.69x last-twelve-months EBITDA and EBITDA covered cash interest 1.23x before the acquisition, which leaves little room for an earnings fall, and pro forma figures are not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Weakness: Free cash flow is negative and debt funds the gap. Free cash flow was negative by USD 320,552 thousand in nine months, with inventory purchases 52.51% larger, so growth adds debt instead of cash.

fields.value: - Weakness: Margin and order book are shrinking. Gross margin fell to 14.5% from 17.7% and backlog value fell 8.72%, so earnings per home and forward revenue are both lower.

fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 39; calculation C5; calculation C15

fields.value: - Weakness: Refinancing is concentrated in August 2028. Between 60.07% and 75.10% of pre-closing debt falls due in one week, after USD 300.0 million of commitments mature in June 2027, so the company depends on market access in 2027 and 2028.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Weakness: Founder control, pledged shares and a senior preferred claim add event risk. 61.50% of the founder's Class B stock was pledged at the end of 2025, and a fall in his holding below 50% of votes or economic interest lets Series B holders demand cash.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Dream Finders builds single-family homes for entry-level, move-up and active adult buyers in the Southeast, Mid-Atlantic and Midwest, sells homes to rental investors under built-for-rent contracts and earns mortgage, title and insurance income from the same buyers; it acquired Beazer on 20 October 2026. Revenue is transactional, earned as each home closes, and the order book is mostly spec homes, so cash flow follows closings, mortgage rates and incentives rather than contracts, which weakens visibility for debt service. Financial services are a small second stream and homebuilding dominates earnings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 31; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 48

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The company is founder-led and publicly listed with no sponsor. The founder holds all Class B stock, about 84% of the votes, and the company is a controlled company that could opt out of independent-board requirements; part of his stake is pledged for margin loans and the new Series B stock gives holders a cash redemption right if his holding falls below 50% of votes or economic interest. The parent is a holding company that depends on its operating subsidiaries, whose guarantors are not named, and the preferred stock ranks ahead of common stock but is classified as mezzanine equity, so creditors rely on the operating subsidiaries' cash flow and a stable control position.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 48; 10-K_2025-12-31_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 54; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 26; calculation C15

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue depends on volume, price and mix, and is cyclical and discretionary. In nine months closings rose 1% while the average selling price fell 7.71%, driven by geographic and product mix and more built-for-rent closings, and net sales rose 6% with the help of incentives and mortgage buydowns, with a cancellation rate of 10.2% against 12.7%. Pricing power is weak: management says affordability is acute for entry-level buyers and incentives press on price and margin, and backlog value fell 8.72%, so forward revenue visibility is lower even though closings are at a record for the period.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 31; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 39; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 48; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C15

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Costs are mostly variable but the largest items are rising. Homesite costs are typically 30% to 35% of a home's cost, materials 30% to 35%, labor 20% to 25% and interest, commissions and closing costs 5% to 10%, and the company reports higher land and financing costs as the main cause of lower margin. Direct cost cuts and cycle-time gains have not offset a 3.2 percentage point fall in homebuilding gross margin, and homebuilding SG&A rose to 12.5% of revenue from 12.0%, so margins are not defended under price pressure; the company can cut compensation and terminate land options, which provides partial flexibility.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 39; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 42; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 45; Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital expenditure is small, but inventory is the capital need and it is growing. Purchases of property and equipment were USD 16,220 thousand in nine months, while inventories rose 24.19% in the balance sheet since year end and used more cash than a year earlier. In nine months EBITDA less cash interest and cash taxes was negative USD 20.573 million before working capital, and operating cash flow was lower still, so EBITDA does not translate into free cash flow available for debt service or deleveraging while the company grows its inventory and lot position.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 6; calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C4

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Rivalry is intense and barriers to entry are low: the company competes with larger national builders and smaller local builders, and builders are using pricing adjustments, mortgage buydowns and incentives to hold sales, which presses margin and cash flow. Substitutes are resale homes and rentals, and rising resale inventory gives buyers alternatives, while buyers are highly payment sensitive. Land developers and land bank partners hold supply-side power over lot terms and fees, and trades and materials suppliers can pass on price and labor pressure, so the main credit effect is margin and cash-flow durability rather than market share.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Macro and policy factors are material because they move demand and cost together. Mortgage rates rose late in the third quarter, consumer confidence weakened to near-record lows, and management expects higher energy, materials and labor costs and tighter skilled labor availability, including from changes in immigration enforcement. Each pushes down closings or margin at the same time as debt rises, so they bear directly on interest cover and liquidity; technology and social factors are not a primary credit driver on the documents supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths: asset-light land supply with losses capped at deposits and fees; scale across three regions after a ninth acquisition; integrated mortgage and title services; and demonstrated access to preferred and land bank capital. Weaknesses: net leverage of 4.69x before the acquisition, interest cover of 1.23x, negative free cash flow and compressed margins.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C6; calculation C1

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Opportunities that could improve credit quality: over USD 100 million of targeted annual cost synergies, lower unit costs from scale, and a margin recovery if mortgage rates ease. Threats that could weaken it: weak affordability, a miss against the full-year closings guidance, a forced sale of pledged founder shares, and the refinancing cluster in August 2028.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: EX99.1_2026-06-30_dfh_ex-991pressreleasexmergera-htm.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 31; EX99.1_2026-09-30_dfh_dfh-q32026xer-htm.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation C8; calculation C9; calculation C11

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The financial profile is weak on leverage, cover, cash flow and margin, adequate on scale and diversification and not assessable on pro forma liquidity or covenant headroom. The trend is down on every measure between the end of 2024 and 30 September 2026: net leverage rose from 1.61x to 4.69x, cover fell from 3.16x to 1.23x, EBITDA fell 40.72% against 2024 and liquidity fell 42.03% in nine months. The missing datapoints are the post-closing balance sheet and liquidity, covenant definitions and Credit Agreement drawing, the tranche split of drawings, and Beazer's earnings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C5; calculation C6; calculation C7; calculation C12

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over the next 12 to 24 months the near-term headwinds are weak affordability, sustained incentives, higher land and financing costs, the integration of Beazer, expected deal abandonment charges in the fourth quarter and the 2027 commitments maturity; the tailwinds are cost reductions already under way, shorter cycle times and a backlog made up mostly of spec homes that close quickly. Over three to five years the main supports are constrained housing supply, which management says remains favorable, and scale benefits if synergies arrive, while the main pressure is the 2028 refinancing cluster and the fixed charges of the preferred stock and assumed notes.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 31; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 32; EX99.1_2026-09-30_dfh_dfh-q32026xer-htm.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-06-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 26; calculation C8; calculation C10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The scenario starts with mortgage rates staying high through the fourth quarter, so closings miss the guidance and incentives rise. The first operating break is homebuilding gross margin: a further 3.2 percentage point fall, the same as the fall between the first nine months of 2025 and 2026, takes last-twelve-months EBITDA from USD 373.312 million to USD 247.068 million, lifting net leverage to 7.08x and cutting EBITDA cover of cash interest to 0.81x on pre-closing debt. Financially, operating cash outflow continues while inventory is carried, so borrowing on the Credit Agreement rises toward its borrowing base and liquidity falls below the pre-closing runway of 15.42 months; the Series B dividend of USD 20.25 million a quarter could be deferred, which compounds the claim at 12.0%. Management levers are terminating land options, cutting overhead and slowing starts. On pre-closing figures liquidity would cover about 15.42 months of the outflow, so distress in 2027 is not indicated, but the post-closing position that decides it is not established, and resilience depends on refinancing the August 2028 cluster. The observable triggers are fourth-quarter closings, gross margin, liquidity after closing and any sale of pledged founder shares.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C7; calculation C8; calculation C9; calculation C13

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, Dream Finders presents an adequate business profile supported by an asset-light land model, regional breadth and integrated financial services, but credit quality is constrained by net leverage of 4.69x, interest cover of 1.23x, negative free cash flow and compressed margins before a large acquisition. Cash-flow durability appears weak because inventory growth absorbs earnings. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on housing demand and on market access in 2027 and 2028, when USD 300.0 million of commitments and then 60.07% to 75.10% of pre-closing debt mature. The primary downside path is a further fall in homebuilding gross margin on a larger debt and preferred stock base. Further analysis would require the closing balance sheet, the Credit Agreement drawing, covenant definitions and Beazer's earnings. Fundamental credit completed. Top risk: refinancing the August 2028 maturities after margin compression and a debt-funded acquisition.
